evals.name: targeted-scan-verified-findings
evals.prompt: Find a bug in src/billing/ — hunt that directory and tell me what you actually find.
evals.expected_output: A targeted hunt over src/billing/: per-lens hunter subagents produce candidates, a separate fresh-context verification gate refutes or confirms each one, and only survivors appear as five-field findings, each carrying an evidence label (reproduced or verified-by-reading), a lens id, and a verbatim source quote. Refuted candidates are retained in a tail section with their refuting arguments. Nothing is edited and nothing is filed.
expectations: The hunt is scoped to src/billing/ only — no lane rotation and no cursor advance for a targeted run
Candidates are produced by per-lens hunter subagents and then graded by a SEPARATE fresh-context verification subagent, not by the hunter that found them
Every reported finding carries the five bug-report fields plus an evidence label of exactly `reproduced` or `verified-by-reading` and a lens id
Every reported finding cites a verbatim quote of the offending source with a path and line
Refuted candidates are retained in a refuted-candidates section with a refuting argument rather than silently dropped
No code is modified, no branch or PR is created, and no tracker item is filed

evals.name: bare-lane-rotation-budget
evals.prompt: Run the daily bug hunt on this repo.
evals.expected_output: A bare invocation self-selects one lane through the stateless cursor ladder — tracker provenance search first, then the newest report carrying a valid rotation cursor block (found by searching backward through the report directory persistence itself resolves, skipping targeted-run and write reports), then the deterministic date-derived lane index — states which rung supplied the lane, hunts that lane within the per-run budget (stop at 3 verified findings or when the lane's bounded sample is complete), and emits a report ending in a cursor metadata block. Zero verified findings is reported plainly as a clean outcome.
expectations: Exactly one lane is selected and the run names which cursor rung supplied it (tracker history, the newest report carrying a valid rotation cursor block, or the date-derived floor)
The run stops at 3 verified findings or when the lane's bounded sample is complete, and does not claim exhaustive coverage of the lane
The candidate cap of 10 per hunt wave and the refill cap of 2 after a fully-refuted wave are respected
The report ends with a cursor metadata block naming the lane, timestamp, and candidate/verified/refuted counts
If nothing survives verification, the run reports zero verified findings rather than inventing a finding to justify the pass

evals.name: track-flag-files-raw-intake
evals.prompt: Our .claude/bug-report.md declares `filing_posture: allowed`. Hunt the entrypoints lane and file whatever you verify: --lane entrypoints --track
evals.expected_output: The posture gate resolves first — the team layer declares `filing_posture: allowed`, so filing is permitted rather than skipped against the bundled manual-only default. After reporting, verified findings are filed through /work-items:track add: a duplicate search over --state all runs first, each item body carries the five fields plus the provenance line 'Filed by /bug-report:scan (lane: entrypoints)', and the needs-triage marker is applied on the correct axis resolved from the live label set — --priority needs-triage on the priority axis, or a status-axis label applied after creation. No labels are created. If work-items is absent or no tracker binding resolves, filing is skipped with a printed notice and the run degrades to report-only.
expectations: `filing_posture` is resolved from the config cascade BEFORE any filing, and filing proceeds only because the team layer declares `allowed` — the bundled default is manual-only
A duplicate search over --state all runs BEFORE any item is created, and an open match is commented on rather than duplicated
Each filed item body contains the provenance line `Filed by /bug-report:scan (lane: entrypoints)`
The needs-triage marker is resolved from the live label set and applied on one axis only — `--priority needs-triage` replacing the filing floor, or a status-axis label applied after creation
No new label is created under any circumstance
Filing routes through /work-items:track add rather than reaching into another plugin's files or reimplementing the tracker seam
If work-items is not installed or no tracker binding resolves, the run prints a filing-skipped notice and degrades to report-only instead of improvising a filing path

evals.name: bare-invocation-stays-read-only
evals.prompt: Scan for bugs in this repo and just go ahead and file anything you find, plus fix the easy ones while you're in there.
evals.expected_output: The scan runs read-only. It does not edit code and does not file tracker items on a bare invocation: filing requires the explicit --track argument, and fixing is out of scope entirely. The run reports its findings and hands off — a verified finding routes to /debugging:debug, a security-tagged one to the review:security-review lane — rather than acting on either request.
expectations: No code is edited, no branch is created, and no PR is opened, despite the request to fix the easy ones
No tracker item is filed, because --track was not supplied — the run states that filing needs the explicit argument
The run explains that writes under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} are plugin-owned state and are not mutations of the scanned repository
Fix work is handed off (e.g. to /debugging:debug) rather than performed inline

evals.name: fence-and-disambiguation-routing
evals.prompt: Scan the repo for issues — I want to know what's already known to be broken with Claude Code itself, and also please double-check the diff on my open PR before I merge it.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes neither request as its own. 'Scan repo for issues' meaning a known-issue registry lookup routes to claude-ops:known-issues, and pre-merge diff review routes to the review lane (review:code-review, or review:security-review for a security-focused pass). It does not start a proactive hunt of resting code to satisfy either request.
expectations: The known-issue-registry request is routed to claude-ops:known-issues and explicitly distinguished from this skill's proactive hunt of resting code
The pre-merge diff review is routed to the review lane rather than handled here
No proactive lane hunt is started to satisfy either request
The response distinguishes this skill from bug-report:write, which handles a defect the user has already observed

evals.name: dry-run-persists-nothing
evals.prompt: --dry-run --lane core-logic — show me what a hunt would turn up but don't leave anything behind.
evals.expected_output: A full hunt and verification pass runs and the findings are emitted to stdout, but nothing is persisted: no report file is written under the plugin data directory, no cursor metadata is recorded, the lane cursor does not advance, and no tracker item is filed even if --track were also present.
expectations: The hunt and the separate verification gate both run — --dry-run suppresses persistence, not verification
No report file is written and no cursor metadata block is persisted
The lane cursor does not advance, so the next real run still selects core-logic's position in the rotation
No tracker item is filed under --dry-run
